messages:
emily: Thinking out loud — what if we add a DelegatedShardLoader that can serve partial byte-range reads for shards and delegate to a merge/streaming loader on misses? Tradeoffs around atomicity and warmup heuristics to discuss.
ryan: Sketch the API pls — curious about failure modes and how fallback looks.
mike: Also how does this play with safetensors index-first / header-first assumptions? partial reads could break some validators.
emily: Rough API idea:
```python
class DelegatedShardLoader:
    def read_range(self, shard_id: str, start: int, end: int) -> bytes:
        """Return bytes for range or raise FallbackNeeded"""
    def validate_header(self, shard_id: str) -> bool:
        """Quick header check (compact) to decide native vs delegate"""
```
mike: ok. If we allow partial reads we need a tiny, deterministic header present at start of file — per-chunk checksums so reader can trust slices without full manifest.
emily: Exactly. Proposal: embed a compact header (~1-2KB) with version, chunk count, 32-bit checksums, signature and key id. Cheap to fetch and verify before delegating.
lee: What about eviction races? Loader could ask remote for chunk A while local evicts B which was a dependency; we might create inconsistency windows. Need generation IDs or TTL-based staleness checks.
ryan: And KV cache warmup implications — partial chunking may leave activations sparse, causing cache thrashing and perf regressions for short sequences. We should measure warmup hit-rate delta.
emily: Heuristic idea: on a partial-read miss, prefetch up/down N adjacent chunks (configurable), but cap by latency budget. If prefetch pushes over SLO, fall back to streaming-only for that model instance. Also allow adaptive backoff if fallback rate > X%.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started: delegated-loader v0.1 on canary pool (tag: canary/d-shard-2026-03-21).
mike: Good — add a chaos test: mid-read connection drop and ensure the fallback path never exposes mixed-weight state (no half-applied chunk).
emily: Agreed. We'll require atomic swap semantics at the consumer boundary: either reader gets fully validated set of chunks for that layer or it triggers fallback to a known-good variant. Also adding a manifest-level generation field to detect concurrent updates.
ryan: Telemetry we should record: partial_read_ratio, fallback_rate, avg_prefix_latency, prefetch_bytes, signature_verification_failures. These will help tune thresholds.
lee: One more: signature verification for header is mandatory for Private deployments — KMS/HSM integration for key lookup. We should include key_id in header so runtime can resolve.
emily: Header sketch (inline):
```json
{"version":"1","shard_id":"abcd1234","chunks":64,"chunk_checksums":["c1","c2",...],"signature":"BASE64SIG","key_id":"awskms://alias/rw-model-keys"}
```
mike: compatibility note: reader should demux .safetensors, legacy .bin and our new header. Ideally call `DelegatedShardLoader.validate_header()` and if false, fall back to existing full-manifest path.
emily: Plan: I'll draft an RFC follow-up with API surface, header spec, failure-mode tests, and canary checklist. Will tag @ryan @mike @lee. Opt-in runtime flag: `--delegated-shard-loader=on|off` and per-model ttl/heuristics config.
ryan: :thumbsup: include perf gate: rollback if fallback_rate > 5% or seq-latency P95 regresses by >10%.
lee: And add an integration test that runs with KMS stub + corrupt signature to ensure we deny delegation.
emily: Will do. I'll put a draft up by EOD and link the test plan. Thanks all. :sparkles:
